questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 -297, -294, -291, -288, -285, -282, ?, -276
questions.solution:
Each term is 3 more than the previous one: -297, -294, -291, -288, -285, -282, ?, -276.
Missing term $= -282 + 3 = -279$, and $-279 + 3 = -276$ ✓.
**Answer: -279**

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

-69, -142, ?, -580, -1164, -2332, -4668, -9340
questions.solution:
Each term is obtained by doubling the previous term and subtracting 4: $2 \times (-69) - 4 = -142$.
Missing term $= 2 \times (-142) - 4 = -288$; check: $2 \times (-288) - 4 = -580$ ✓, and the chain continues up to $-9340$ ✓.
**Answer: -288**

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

 -33, ?, -202, -405, -1216, -2433, -7300
questions.solution:
The operations alternate: multiply by 2 and subtract 1, then multiply by 3 and subtract 1.
$-33 \times 2 - 1 = -67$; $-67 \times 3 - 1 = -202$; $-202 \times 2 - 1 = -405$; $-405 \times 3 - 1 = -1216$; $-1216 \times 2 - 1 = -2433$; $-2433 \times 3 - 1 = -7300$ ✓.
Missing term $= -67$.
**Answer: -67**

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

Z, ?, J, O, T, Y, D, I
questions.solution:
From J onwards every letter moves 5 places ahead: J, O, T, Y, D, I (cycling back after Z).
So the missing letter is 5 places after Z, which is E, and E $+ 5$ = J ✓.
Series: Z, E, J, O, T, Y, D, I.
**Answer: E**
questions.shortcut: Uniform gap of +5 places; E completes the chain Z - E - J - O - T - Y - D - I.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

Q, S, V, X, ?, C, F, H
questions.solution:
The gaps between letters alternate +2 and +3: Q(+2) S(+3) V(+2) X(+3) ? (+2) C(+3) F(+2) H.
After X, +3 places gives 27, which wraps to A; then A $+ 2$ = C ✓.
**Answer: A**

questions.q: If the 1st of a month is Wednesday, then what will be the 29th day of that month?
questions.solution:
The 29th day is 28 days after the 1st, and 28 days = exactly 4 weeks.
So the 29th falls on the same weekday as the 1st, i.e. Wednesday.
**Answer: Wednesday**
questions.shortcut: 1st + 28 days (4 weeks) always lands on the same weekday.

questions.q: In the year 1925, which of the following month had 5 Thursdays?
questions.solution:
A 31-day month gets five of a weekday only when that weekday falls on the 1st, 2nd or 3rd of the month.
1 January 1925 was a Thursday, so January had Thursdays on 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29 - five Thursdays.
February 1925 had only 28 days (four of every weekday), and March and May 1925 also had only four Thursdays.
**Answer: January**
questions.shortcut: 1 January 1925 was a Thursday and January has 31 days, giving five Thursdays.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
questions.solution:
Two years have identical calendars when 1 January falls on the same weekday in both years and both are of the same type (both ordinary or both leap).
1 January 1914 and 1 January 1925 both fell on a Thursday, and both are ordinary years, so 1914 and 1925 have identical calendars.
The other pairs fail: 1924 and 1912 are leap years while 1911 and 1906 are not, and 1 January 1911 (Sunday) does not match 1 January 1929 (Tuesday).
**Answer: 1914 and 1925**
questions.shortcut: Same calendar = same 1 January weekday + same leap/ordinary type; 1914 and 1925 both start on Thursday.

questions.q: 5 boys A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). No one is to the left of D. Only 3 boys are to the right of B. A is to the immediate left of E and immediate right of C. Who is to the immediate right of B?
questions.solution:
D has no one to his left, so D takes the extreme left seat. Only 3 boys are to the right of B, so B is in the second seat.
A is to the immediate left of E and immediate right of C, so C-A-E together fill seats 3, 4 and 5.
Row: D, B, C, A, E - the boy immediately to the right of B is C.
**Answer: C**
questions.shortcut: Fix D at seat 1 and B at seat 2; C-A-E must fill the remaining three seats in order.

questions.q: 7 boys P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). V is second to the right of R . U is to immediate left of R . P is third to the right of T . S and T are the immediate neighbours of Q . Who is sitting third to the right of V ?
questions.solution:
With everyone facing the centre, a move to the right goes anti-clockwise and a move to the left goes clockwise.
Fix R. U is to R's immediate left and V is second to R's right. S and T must sit on the two sides of Q, and P is third to T's right - the only seating that fits every clue is (clockwise): R, U, T, Q, S, V, P.
Counting 3 seats to the right of V (anti-clockwise) lands on T.
**Answer: T**

questions.q: 7 women A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). F is second to the right of C. A is third to the left of C. G is third to the left of F. D is not next to F. B is not next to A. Considering towards left of A, how many women are sitting between A and E?
questions.solution:
With everyone facing the centre, left = clockwise and right = anti-clockwise.
Fix C. F is second to C's right, A is third to C's left and G is third to F's left. D cannot sit next to F and B cannot sit next to A, which forces the clockwise order: C, G, D, A, E, F, B.
Going left (clockwise) from A, the very next woman is E, so no one sits between A and E.
**Answer: 0**

In TQ200 : US320 the letters shift +1 and +2 places (T to U, Q to S) and the number increases by 120 (200 to 320).
KP150 : LR270 confirms the same rule (K to L, P to R, 150 to 270).
Applying it to AD120: A to B, D to F, and $120 + 120 = 240$, giving BF240.
**Answer: BF240**
questions.shortcut: Letters +1/+2, number +120, so AD120 becomes BF240.

questions.q: Select the option that is related to WSR280 in the same way as ZAW480 is related to ACZ120 and XVS670 is related to YXV310.
questions.solution:
In ACZ120 : ZAW480 each letter moves back 1, 2 and 3 places (A to Z, C to A, Z to W) and the number increases by 360 (120 to 480).
YXV310 : XVS670 confirms it: Y to X, X to V, V to S, and $310 + 360 = 670$.
Applying the same to WSR280: W to V, S to Q, R to O, and $280 + 360 = 640$, giving VQO640.
**Answer: VQO640**

questions.q:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Dairy

2. Daily

3. Daintly

4. Daisy

5. Dais
questions.solution:
All the words begin with DAI, so the 4th letter decides the order: Daily (L), Daintly (N), Dairy (R), Dais and Daisy (S).
Dictionary order: Daily (2), Daintly (3), Dairy (1), then Dais (5) before Daisy (4), because 'Dais' stops earlier.
Sequence: 2, 3, 1, 5, 4 = 23154.
**Answer: 23154**
questions.shortcut: 4th letters run L < N < R < S; Dais comes before Daisy.

questions.q:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Forest

2. Foreign

3. Forego

4. Forever

5. Foretaste
questions.solution:
All the words begin with Fore, so the 5th letter decides: Forego (G), Foreign (I), Forest (S), Foretaste (T), Forever (V).
Alphabetical order: Forego (3), Foreign (2), Forest (1), Foretaste (5), Forever (4) = 32154.
**Answer: 32154**
questions.shortcut: 5th letters run G < I < S < T < V.

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

 1740 : 1782 :: 7992 : 8034 :: 9866 : ?
questions.solution:
Each second number is 42 more than the first: $1740 + 42 = 1782$ and $7992 + 42 = 8034$.
So $9866 + 42 = 9908$.
**Answer: 9908**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to fifth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

 469 : ? :: 667 : 2673 :: 958 : 3837
In a certain code language, 'SAD' is coded as ' 27 ' and 'RAID' is coded as ' 35 '. How will 'TABLE' be coded in that code language?
questions.solution:
Add the alphabet positions of all letters, then add 3.
SAD $= 19 + 1 + 4 + 3 = 27$; RAID $= 18 + 1 + 9 + 4 + 3 = 35$.
TABLE $= 20 + 1 + 2 + 12 + 5 + 3 = 43$.
**Answer: 43**

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'MASTER' is coded as '85' and 'CARE' is coded as '80'. How will 'SCHOOL' be coded in that code language?
questions.solution:
Take each letter's position from the reverse alphabet (A = 26, B = 25, ..., Z = 1) and subtract 1 from the total.
MASTER $= 14 + 26 + 8 + 7 + 22 + 9 - 1 = 85$; CARE $= 24 + 26 + 9 + 22 - 1 = 80$.
SCHOOL $= 8 + 24 + 19 + 12 + 12 + 15 - 1 = 90 - 1 = 89$.
**Answer: 89**

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'acodemic marks important' is coded as 'pd rs ln', 'marks shows rank' is coded as 'rs tn pq', and 'rank generate merit' is coded as 'tn lq zx'. How will 'marks rank' be coded in that code language?
questions.solution:
'marks' appears in the first two sentences and 'rs' is the common code word, so marks = rs.
'rank' appears in the last two sentences and 'tn' is the common code word, so rank = tn.
Hence 'marks rank' is coded as 'rs tn'.
**Answer: rs tn**
questions.concept: Coding and Decoding in Fictitious Language
questions.shortcut: The common word takes the common code: marks = rs, rank = tn.
